title: Nitin's 'Nabin' team: BJP hits reset button with eye on UP and 'Mission 2029'
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party has unveiled its dynamic new national team of office-bearers, strategically assembled to tackle both the upcoming assembly elections and the 2029 Lok Sabha contest. This diverse lineup features a mix of seasoned politicians and fresh talent, representing various regions. Some notable figures are making returns, while others have been sidelined, highlighting the party's commitment to revitalizing its organizational framework for future challenges.

title: 100 days of TVK govt: CM Vijay defines priorities, but his real test begins now
content: Tamil Nadu's new Chief Minister Vijay's government has completed its first hundred days.  The administration has focused heavily on welfare programs and social initiatives.  Significant investment commitments have also been secured for the state's development.  The government has implemented measures to address women's safety and curb drug use. But now delivery of these promises will be closely watched.

title: BWF Worlds: Ayush Shetty stuns World No. 1 Shi Yu Qi; India 5-0 on Day 1
content: Ayush Shetty produced the biggest win of his career on Day 1 at the BWF World Championships, stunning top seed and defending champion Shi Yu Qi in a thrilling contest. Led by the young Indian's heroics and PV Sindhu's comfortable win, India made a perfect 5-0 start on the opening day of the tournament in New Delhi.

title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this month
content: Accenture's CEO, Julie Sweet, has requested that employees delay their vacation in August. This temporary policy adjustment is designed to bolster staff presence as the company approaches the end of its financial year. Following disappointing quarterly results and a forecasted drop in revenue, Accenture is permitting employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next fiscal year to help enhance fourth-quarter outputs and revenue generation.

title: ‘Show composure’: Coach’s message to India ahead of must-not-lose Pakistan clash
content: Following India's defeat in the Hockey World Cup, coach Craig Fulton emphasised the necessity for stricter defensive discipline. He urged players to maintain composure and enhance their defensive strategies ahead of the critical match against Pakistan. Midfielder Manpreet Singh echoed his sentiments, pinpointing defensive errors as pivotal to their loss. A point against Pakistan is essential for India's progression to the next round.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40bn in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's philanthropic efforts have made a significant impact by enabling the cancellation of medical debt across the United States. By purchasing and eliminating patient debt at a minimal cost, she has set a precedent that encourages other wealthy individuals to invest in similar initiatives. Despite these immediate acts of generosity, the need for comprehensive policy reforms persists, as true transformation necessitates addressing the fundamental issues leading to medical debt.

title: ‘Pollution is pretty insane’: Antonsen wants India Open to move out of Delhi winter
content: Danish badminton player Anders Antonsen has voiced concerns regarding the BWF's scheduling of the India Open, criticising the January-February timeframe due to the heavy winter pollution in Delhi. He chose to miss this year's tournament, incurring a fine as a result. Antonsen believes that the winter air quality severely hampers athletes' performance and calls for improved conditions in future competitions.

title: Hawaii’s 1905 mosquitofish import now linked to native species decline
content: The introduction of mosquitofish in Hawaii has dramatically affected the ecosystem, leading to notable declines in native aquatic insects. These invasive fish fiercely prey on local species, disrupting food chains. The native damselflies, unprepared for such predation, are particularly vulnerable, seeing their populations plummet. Additionally, mosquitofish compete with endemic fish and crustaceans for limited food resources, complicating control efforts due to intricate waterways and their fast breeding habits.

title: David and Victoria Beckham win planning battle at £6.15m Cotswolds home
content: David and Victoria Beckham have won permission for ‘Blackpool-style’ lake illuminations, a hot tub and firepit at their £6.15 million Cotswolds home, despite objections from a critic living in Australia. The planning approval comes with conditions, including a ban on motorised boats and restrictions on firepit use during bird-nesting season at the estate.

title: US student wins award for geometry breakthrough: How it can change modern medicine
content: Connor Hill won first place at the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search competition.  His research classified noble polyhedra, identifying two infinite families and 146 isolated examples.  Hill translated a geometric problem into a finite algebraic one for a complete classification.  This method of reducing complexity is vital for modern biology and drug discovery.  His work demonstrates how mathematical simplification aids understanding in complex scientific fields.

title: 'Let me die in peace right now': Chargesheet reveals Twisha's chilling final message
content: The CBI's chargesheet highlights the alleged cruelty faced by Twisha Sharma at the hands of her husband and mother-in-law, who reportedly inflicted mental and psychological torment during their union. Notably, Twisha communicated a final message to her sister-in-law shortly before her passing. The post-mortem revealed that her demise resulted from suicide via ante-mortem hanging, with investigations ongoing as forensic data from devices and CCTV footage is awaited.

title: WC: India coach questions FIH over China’s penalty stroke, later deletes posts
content: Indian women's hockey coach questioned the penalty-stroke rule interpretation after a draw.  He shared footage and sought clarification from the International Hockey Federation.  Former players also expressed their views on the controversial penalty-stroke action.  The coach later removed his social media posts regarding the incident.  FIH had not responded to clarification requests at the time of publication.

title: Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4: Collaborations, battle pass and everything we know
content: Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 Override is set to launch on August 20, 2026, introducing players to a new Battle Pass. The map will experience significant revisions, with several points of interest being replaced by fresh locations. Fans will be thrilled to see the introduction of eight new Sprites, including Sonic and Tails, along with exciting new weaponry such as the 8-Bit Shotgun and Masamune Assault Rifle.

title: From Charles Haley to Von Miller: Jerry Jones’ history of backing controversial stars
content: Jerry Jones champions the idea of second chances in football, seeing promise in players with troubled backgrounds. Charles Haley’s journey with the Dallas Cowboys resulted in three Super Bowl glories, showcasing the impact of rehabilitation. Now, the  signing of Von Miller shines a light on this philosophy, as he too carries a controversial past alongside two Super Bowl triumphs, challenging Jones’ belief in restorative player management.

title: What did Braelon Allen fear after Breece Hall suffered a suspected groin injury?
content: In a recent practice session, New York Jets RB Breece Hall may have incurred a groin injury, raising eyebrows among players. RB2 Braelon Allen, who managed to score a touchdown, voiced both his worries and relief. Hall had just secured a hefty contract extension, so attention is high. Coach Aaron Glenn reassured fans, suggesting the injury might be minor, pending more thorough evaluations.

title: 'It's a lady's sport': The challenge of badminton in Uganda, Canada, Bulgaria
content: The 2026 BWF World Championships highlight badminton’s global reach, with top representation from Asian powerhouses and Denmark. While nations like Bulgaria, Uganda, and South Africa have fewer athletes and limited resources, their stories underscore dedication and growth.

title: House rent in most EU capitals exceed minimum wage
content: In numerous EU capitals, rent prices outstrip the minimum wage, significantly impacting low-income earners. Cities like Prague and Lisbon record the highest rent-to-income ratios, especially for two-bedroom apartments. Other capitals also indicate rental costs above the gross monthly minimum wage. However, Brussels and Berlin provide relatively affordable housing options for those earning minimum wage. The escalating housing expenses continue to be a critical issue for workers across Europe.

title: Hockey WC: India’s 32-year England jinx continues as late goals seal 2-4 defeat
content: England secured a 4-2 victory over India in their Hockey World Cup Pool D match. India led 2-1 at halftime after goals from Harmanpreet and Dilpreet Singh. England responded strongly in the second half, scoring three times to seal the win. This defeat means India must draw against Pakistan to advance. The result extends India's winless streak against England in the World Cup.

title: Suthar and Jadeja's first date at Galle: Past continuous, future perfect
content: Ravindra Jadeja's relentless consistency and Suthar's wrist and finger magic combined to give India a glimpse of a potent left-arm spin partnership in Galle. With seven wickets between them, the duo offered India a template that bridges the present and the future.

title: ONGC gets US licence to expand Venezuela operations, boost oil output
content: ONGC has successfully obtained approval from the US Treasury, allowing it to further extend its oil operations in Venezuela. The newly acquired license significantly reduces sanctions-related barriers, paving the way for increased investments and production capabilities. With this development, ONGC can explore new contracts and possibly take over projects from PDVSA.

title: ‘Jana Nayagan’ OTT: When and where to watch Vijay’s final film
content: Jana Nayagan, the much-anticipated final film of Vijay, is set to premiere on Zee5 starting August 21. This political action drama has garnered a varied reception but has enjoyed strong box office success. Despite facing numerous obstacles prior to its release, the film achieved impressive global earnings. Fans can now enjoy Vijay's poignant farewell from the comfort of their homes.

title: Smriti Irani's big comeback: Why BJP has turned to its 'giant killer'
content: Smriti Irani is reappointed as a general secretary for the BJP's national team, a move that highlights the party's strategic push in Uttar Pradesh ahead of upcoming elections. Following setbacks in the recent Lok Sabha elections, her previous success in Amethi positions her as a critical asset. This role will see her coordinating with state units and overseeing candidate selections.

title: Zoya Akhtar confirms 'Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara 2' with Hrithik, Farhan and Abhay
content: Zoya Akhtar confirmed 'Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara 2' is in development with Reema Kagti, though its future remains uncertain until the right story emerges. A 2025 ad reignited fan buzz. Zoya also dismissed criticism about her films focusing on privileged characters, defending her creative freedom to tell varied stories.

title: No new strikes, no peace deal: What Donald Trump’s ‘low-key’ Iran strategy means
content: The United States is employing a low-key strategy against Iran after a deadline expired. Economic pressure and diplomacy are now the primary tools being utilized. The US is maintaining sanctions and a naval blockade to influence Tehran. This approach aims to avoid immediate military escalation while seeking concessions. Backchannel communications continue as both sides assess their leverage.

title: Cong workers sing 2 stanzas of Vande Mataram at Goa rally; Kharge attacks BJP
content: During a recent meeting in Goa, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge passionately led a rendition of Vande Mataram, addressing BJP workers who protested against his convoy, alleging disrespect. In response, Kharge challenged the BJP's claims about patriotism, reminding attendees of the party's historical connections to the British Empire. This demonstration came amidst a new directive from the Union home ministry regarding the proper performance of the national song.

title: DU suspends PhD scholar for slapping professor, bars campus entry; CCTV video emerges
content: Delhi University has taken decisive action by suspending a PhD scholar from its law faculty. Following allegations of an assault on a professor earlier this week, the scholar has also been prohibited from entering university premises effective immediately. The incident, which was captured on CCTV showing the scholar slapping the professor, will now be investigated by an independent committee to ensure accountability and transparency.

title: Kangana Ranaut on 'Bharat Bhagya Vidhaata': 'Patriotism has many forms'
content: Kangana Ranaut discussed 'Bharat Bhagya Vidhaata', saying patriotism extends beyond soldiers to doctors, nurses and ordinary citizens who act with courage. She hopes the film teaches younger generations that heroism exists in everyday choices, not just grand moments. The film, directed by Manoj Tapadia, is now streaming on Zee5.

title: Shabnam Sinha to succeed Sunil Bharti Mittal as Airtel Payments Bank chairperson
content: Shabnam Sinha is set to take over as chairperson of Airtel Payments Bank starting October 1. With Sunil Bharti Mittal concluding his term as non-executive chairman on September 30, 2026, Sinha's appointment is timely. As an independent director with profound leadership credentials, she intends to leverage the bank's substantial growth and enhance digital banking access throughout India, reinforcing its commitment to innovation and expansion.

title: Jadeja scripts history with 350th wicket, joins Kapil, Botham, Vettori in elite club
content: Ravindra Jadeja achieved a significant career milestone in Test cricket. He became the fourth player ever to score 4,000 runs and take 350 wickets. This remarkable feat was accomplished during the first Test against Sri Lanka. Jadeja joins an elite group of all-rounders with this achievement. His efficiency is highlighted by reaching this landmark in under 100 matches.

title: Once plagued by elephant raids, Assam village now grows grass & fruits for wild herds
content: In Hatikhuli-Ronghang village, a remarkable relationship with wild elephant herds has blossomed. By establishing dedicated feeding zones, the community effectively reduces crop damage and tackles food shortages along traditional elephant migration routes. This transformation has allowed farmers to resume paddy cultivation, fostering a newfound harmony between humans and elephants. The Hati Bondhu initiative beautifully illustrates the potential for peaceful coexistence between culture and wildlife.

title: Jayden Daniels’ LSU controversy takes a new turn ahead of the new season
content: Jayden Daniels' LSU controversy has now taken a new turn as ESPN's analyst has reacted to it while the star player gets brutally trolled.

title: “Kelce needs to be respectful”: Travis Kelce faces backlash over anthem behavior
content: Travis Kelce sparked controversy during the Kansas City Chiefs’ 2025 game against Washington after cameras showed him moving energetically during the national anthem. Some viewers called his behavior disrespectful, while others defended him as simply warming up with his hand over his heart. His 2017 decision to kneel during the anthem also resurfaced, adding fuel to the debate. Kelce later delivered a standout performance, helping Kansas City secure a 28-7 victory.

title: Missiles below, mountains ahead: How the IAF had to improvise in the middle of war
content: The Indian Air Force conducted a unique high-altitude air-to-ground campaign during the 1999 Kargil conflict.  Fighter pilots faced unprecedented challenges fighting at altitudes of 14-18,000 feet.  Early losses prompted tactical changes and accelerated the integration of precision-guided munitions.  The conflict highlighted India's need for indigenous navigation technology and satellite systems.  Lessons learned from Kargil continue to shape India's military innovation and preparedness.

title: Seven dead in stampede at temple in Bihar’s Lakhisarai
content: Eyewitnesses say that two trains full of devotees had reached Lakhisarai railway station, and the devotees, mostly women, rushed to offer Ganga water to Lord Shiva; they add that the stampede happened due to lack of crowd management and rumour of an electric pole snapping

content: The fire erupted around 4.30 a.m. on the ground floor of the four-storey hotel in the temple town of Tarapith, when most of the guests were asleep. Out of the eight deceased, five were from Garo Hills of Meghalaya and three were from Alipurduar district of West Bengal.

title: Groundwater that glows yellow-green in U.P.
content: Decades of industrial waste dumping have contaminated groundwater with chromium (VI) across parts of three Uttar Pradesh districts, exposing villagers to unsafe water and serious health risks. Despite years of complaints and court intervention, the government’s efforts to identify contaminated areas, provide safe drinking water and healthcare, and clean up toxic waste remain slow and inadequate.

content: a US Navy guided-missile destroyer spent four days without working toilets, galley services . the ship suffered an "engineering casualty involving its generators," a spokesperson says . no injuries were reported aboard the ship in the south china sea .

content: IRGC denies the claim that the united states was engaged in backchannel talks with the force over the war . the reported channel was facilitated in part by the iraqi president . a spokesperson for barzani confirmed to Iran international that he had helped relay messages between Washington and Tehran .

title: 'Follow law of land': Centre to X after Musk's new rule on govt censorship requests
content: X users will be able to see when governments seek the removal of posts or request restrictions on accounts . the social media platform introduced a new rule to make government-driven restrictions on content more visible to users . "X will have to follow the law of the land," the officer said .

title: Big win for students: J'khand govt scraps JSSC-CGL exam, all tests via TDPL since 2014
content: JSSC and jharkhand cancelled 14th and backlog exams as protests entered 24th day with 6 on hunger strike . the move came after the agitation, led by the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, demanded a probe into alleged irregularities . most of the demands made by the students have now been accepted by the government .
